title: Test Diverse Users
outcome: By the end, I can evaluate varied case types and prioritise an important failure slice.
scenario: A fictional recommender is tested on distinct ordinary, equality, invalid-input and tie cases.
given: Recorded full passes: ordinary 4/4; equality 1/3; invalid 2/3; ties 1/2.
Categories are disjoint and every case was run on the same frozen version with the same contract.

steps.label: Prioritise repair
steps.detail: Inspect failed equality traces and any invalid-input safety consequence, not only the total.

explanation: Varied tests expose behavior an ordinary demonstration misses. The overall result combines disjoint cases once each; overlapping labels would require unique-case accounting. Prioritisation also depends on consequences: a malformed input that triggers an unauthorised action can be more serious than a harmless tie-order failure. Retain each failed case and its expected output.

counterfactual.change: Someone reports only the ordinary slice.
counterfactual.prediction: The claim becomes 4/4 on ordinary cases, not 100% across all tests.
counterfactual.reason: Eight nonordinary cases and their failures have been omitted.

student_task: Can these records establish performance for different user groups?
teacher_answer: No. They describe input-case types. No user-group membership or group-specific outcomes were supplied.
project_evidence: Build a recommender evaluation matrix with routine, boundary, missing, invalid and tie cases, then add separately planned user-condition coverage.
limits: Twelve designed cases describe this test suite, not an unbiased estimate of future usage accuracy.
review_note: New fictional case individually matched to this topic, with computations and policy traces checked. Use for supported practice; preserve the independent assessment.
